strengths: Comprehensive coverage: 72+ algorithm variants across 13 general-purpose BBO families addresses a significant gap in the Python ecosystem for population-based optimization

Timely focus on large-scale black-box optimization with emphasis on recent advanced techniques (decomposition, low-memory approximation, low-rank metric learning, variance reduction, ensemble methods, self-adaptation, smoothing)
Practical unified API design that integrates cleanly with NumPy/SciPy ecosystem, facilitating accessibility and adoption
Clear positioning relative to existing libraries (COCO, NeverGrad, DEAP, PaGMO) and articulate discussion of complementary scope
Commendable emphasis on reproducibility and code quality, including explicit random seeding and promised repeatability reports
Good motivation grounded in real applications (deep RL policy search, adversarial attacks on neural networks)
Clean, well-organized presentation with helpful usage example demonstrating ease of interface
weaknesses: Complete absence of experimental evaluation: No benchmarking results, performance metrics, or comparative analysis with other libraries or methods. Critical for validating claims about implementation quality and efficiency

Zero empirical validation of key claims: 'elegant implementations,' 'unified API' benefits, and 'computational efficiency' are asserted without evidence. The promised 'code-based repeatability reports' are mentioned but none are presented

Insufficient technical depth for research venue: Framework description is vague; missing architectural details, design rationale, implementation decisions, and performance analysis. Section 3 promises framework details but provides minimal information

Limited novelty: All algorithms are existing implementations. No novel algorithms, theoretical advances, or algorithmic techniques contributed. Contribution is purely software engineering consolidation
No validation of advantages over alternatives: Why should users choose PyPop7 over NeverGrad or DEAP? No comparative performance data, usability study, or feature analysis provided

Missing practical implementation details: How are search space constraints enforced? How are convergence criteria determined? How customizable are individual algorithms? These details critical for usability are absent
No limitations or performance boundary discussion: Paper lacks candid assessment of when methods fail, scalability limits, memory requirements, or performance trade-offs
